title: feat(spec)!: approver and decision-output positions are names from the metadata registry (ADR-0131 D4)
body:
Part of #22682
Clause-②: yes

Items 1 and 2 of the card: the approver `position` binding and the decision-output `position` become names, listed from the metadata registry (ADR-0131 D4). Item 3, the position form's `permissionSets` widget (`packages/spec/src/identity/position.form.ts`), waits for stage 1 of #15204, so #22682 remains open for it. Claim `6098135473`, dispatched by the `domain:spec` seat 2.

## What changes

All in `packages/spec/src/automation/approval.zod.ts`.

1. **`ApproverValueBinding` gains a `registry` member**, `{ source: 'registry'; type: string }`: the value is the machine name of an item of metadata `type`. A picker lists `GET /api/v1/meta/TYPE`, which serves the code-declared and the environment-authored items alike (ADR-0131 D2), and commits the item's `name`.
2. **`APPROVER_VALUE_BINDINGS.position`** is `{ source: 'registry', type: 'position' }`. It was `{ source: 'record', object: 'sys_position', valueField: 'name' }`. The `satisfies` exhaustiveness check, under which every `ApproverType` member needs a binding, is kept.
3. **`APPROVER_VALUE_SOURCES`** projects a `registry` binding onto the wire as its own source, so the approval node schema's `approvers[].value` `xRef.sources.position` reads `{ source: 'registry', type: 'position' }`. Its type gains `{ source: 'registry'; type: string }`. `user`, `team` and `department` still project `data`. The docblock that said the registry "does not hold … `sys_position` ROWS" now says what each source is for: `data` for a directory row, `registry` for a catalog item.
4. **`DecisionOutputDef`'s `position` output collects position machine names.** The docblock said every picker's values were record ids. It now says each picker kind is sourced and committed exactly like the approver type of the same name, and the `type` and `multiple` `.describe()` strings say what each picker commits. The `resolveAs` and node-level `decisionOutputs` docblocks say the same. The generated reference `content/docs/references/automation/approval.mdx` is regenerated (`gen:docs`, the one artifact `check:generated` named).

Departures from the suggested route, both deliberate:

- **No `valueField` on the `registry` member.** A catalog item has no row id; its name is the only reference it has (ADR-0131 D4), so a `valueField` could only ever hold `name`, a key with nothing to choose.
- **`type` is `string`, not `MetadataType`.** Importing the kernel's type, even type-only, pulled `kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts` and about 25 transitive modules into the generated skill reference index (`skills/objectstack-automation/references/_index.md`, a governed `skills/**` path). The import is dropped, and `approval.test.ts` holds every registry binding's `type` to `MetadataTypeSchema` instead.

The runtime does not change. `plugin-approvals` routes a position approver, an escalation target and a `resolveAs: 'position'` value by filtering `sys_user_position.position` by name, and none of it reads the binding.

## Premises, re-verified on `origin/main` `243dd3c625`

- `approval.zod.ts:206` was `position: { source: 'record', object: 'sys_position', valueField: 'name' }`. `APPROVER_VALUE_SOURCES` (`:238`) projected `record` to `{ source: 'data', object, valueField }`. `DecisionOutputDef` (`:576`) read "Picker values are record ids". `approval.test.ts:152`, `:193` and `:210` pinned those shapes.
- **No registry binding kind existed.** The union was `record | enum | auto | trigger-field | expression | unsupported`. `git grep` for `APPROVER_VALUE_BINDINGS`, `APPROVER_VALUE_SOURCES` and `ApproverValueBinding` outside `packages/spec` finds one code reader, `packages/lint/src/validate-approval-approvers.ts:451`, which reads only `source === 'unsupported'` and is unaffected. The only registry-picker spelling elsewhere in the spec is the form-widget `ref:TYPE` vocabulary (`ref:object`, `ref:dataset`, `ref:component`), which is a widget key in `*.form.ts` and not a value binding. It is item 3's layer, so no second vocabulary is introduced here.
- **Item 2's values are already names at run time.** `decideNode` hands outputs to the flow verbatim (`approval-service.ts` `acceptedOutputs`). The one reader that interprets a position value is an `expression` approver with `resolveAs: 'position'`, and that calls `expandPositionUsers(key)`, which filters `sys_user_position` by `position: NAME` (`approval-service.ts:2686`). A `sys_position` id would route the request to nobody. So item 2 is a contract and docblock correction with no value-shape change, and `plugin-approvals` is untouched.

## What objectui at the pinned `.objectui-sha` does with this

Read at objectui `20c6d351ad74` (the pin) with `git show`.

- **objectui bundles `@objectstack/spec@17.7.0` from npm.** Its lockfile resolves that version, and `packages/app-shell` and `packages/fields` declare `^17.6.0`. This change ships on the v18 prerelease line, which `^17` never resolves. So every reader that imports the constant still sees the old binding: `approverIdentity.ts` (`APPROVER_DIRECTORY_BINDINGS`, read by `useApproverDirectory`), `FlowReferenceField.tsx` (`KIND_TO_RECORD_LOOKUP`) and `decisionOutputParams.ts` (`OUTPUT_LOOKUP_OBJECTS`, its own hand-written table).
- **The one reader that takes the binding off the wire** is the flow designer, which reads `xRef.sources` from the approval node schema the server publishes. `sourceOf` in `json-schema-to-fields.ts` accepts only `data`, `enum`, `auto`, `trigger-field`, `expression` and `unsupported`. It drops any other entry by design ("A dropped entry simply leaves the consumer on its local fallback"). `sources.position` is therefore absent, and `recordLookupFor` falls back to the bundled `KIND_TO_RECORD_LOOKUP.position`, a `sys_position` data lookup that commits `name`. That is today's control exactly: no throw and no free-text box, for as long as `sys_position` rows exist.
- **If objectui moves to a spec carrying this change without the C9 follow-up**, `position` drops out of both spec-derived tables, because both keep only `source === 'data'` and skip anything else without throwing. The designer's position cell becomes a combobox with no suggestions, which is the free-text degradation the spec's comment records. `formatIdentity` stops prettifying `position:sales_manager` and middle-truncates it to `positi…ager`, and `useApproverDirectory` stops resolving labels and holders for position seats. Nothing throws.
- **Ordering this implies:** this PR does not need to wait for objectui. The objectui follow-up (objectui#7611 C9) has to land in or before the objectui PR that moves objectui's spec dependency to the v18 line, and before #15204's stage 8 retires `sys_position`, because the pin's fallback lookup reads that object. The seat decides.
- Today's objectui decision dialog builds the position output as a `lookup` on `sys_position` with no `idField`, so it commits the row id. Under the corrected contract that id routes a downstream `resolveAs: 'position'` approver to nobody. That reader is in the C9 follow-up's census (`decisionOutputParams`). This is a code reading, not a reproduction.

## Semver and the migration ledger

- `Clause-②: yes`. The published `ApproverValueBinding` and the `APPROVER_VALUE_SOURCES` type each gain a member, and the `xRef.sources` payload gains the key `type`.
- **BREAKING**, named in the changeset: the published `APPROVER_VALUE_SOURCES.position` entry changes shape for an existing reader. A renderer that keys on `source === 'data'`, as objectui's derived tables do, loses `position` until it reads `registry`. The changeset is `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`. Pre mode is on (tag `next`), and breaking changes ship as `minor` under the launch-window convention, as the stock does.
- ADR-0087 disposition: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. No authorable key, export or stored value moves. A position approver's value and a position decision output were names at run time and stay names, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite.
- `api-surface/` and `export-origins/` are unchanged, because no export is added, removed or renamed. `check:api-surface` and `check:export-origins` pass.

## Tests

The final head is `d4ca8f4762`.

Every run below was taken on that head, after `origin/main` `9646991283` was merged in. Builds and tests ran through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, and each reading is the verdict line it printed.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`, then `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`, the scripts typecheck and the test-layer typecheck): exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`, the whole local suite: **642 test files and 19,161 tests passed, 1 todo.**
- `src/automation/approval.test.ts`: 66 of 66 passed. Changed pins: position binds `{ source: 'registry', type: 'position' }`, and every registry binding's `type` parses under `MetadataTypeSchema`. No binding names `sys_position`. `APPROVER_VALUE_SOURCES.position` is the registry source, and `registry` belongs to `position` alone. The published JSON schema's `xRef.sources.position` is the registry source. Every typed decision-output picker kind is an approver type bound to `record` or `registry`.
- **Consumers, the downstream direction.** The `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` dependency closure was built with turbo (31 of 31 tasks). `@objectstack/lint`'s full suite passed: 135 files, 6,231 tests. Its reader of the bindings needs no change, and the existing "accepts the position approver type … silently" pin holds. The `plugin-approvals` read covered `approval-service.test.ts`, `approval-node.test.ts` and `approver-address-readers.test.ts`: 3 files and 378 tests passed. None of them was edited.
- **Ablation**, run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode on the committed head. The anchor `position: { source: 'registry', type: 'position' },` went from 1 to 0, and the record-binding replacement went from 0 to 1. The blob moved from `ba3680f2ddef` to `5195b44a4161`. `approval.test.ts` then went **red, 3 failed and 63 passed**, in the expected direction: the binding pin, the wire-source pin and the published-schema pin. The tool restored the file: its blob equals HEAD's `ba3680f2ddef`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. A separate `git hash-object` check agrees.
- **Gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (no paths) derives 109 commands on this head. `--ran` with recorded exit codes reconciles **109 derived: 108 run, 1 NOT MEASURED, 0 unrun**.
  - Three gates needed a second run. `check:docs-transcript-drift` had refused for `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, with lint not built yet. `check:query-options-erasure` and `check:type-check-debt` had hit a 300 s runner timeout. All three exit 0 on the second run.
  - `check:skill-examples` and `check:dts-closure` had read `client-react` and `verify` dists that the shared turbo cache replayed without declarations. Both exit 0 after a direct rebuild of those two packages, which this diff does not touch.
  - `check:generated` reports all 15 artifacts up to date. `check:adr-0087-registration` reports 1 declared-breaking changeset with a disposition. `check-changeset-no-major` exits 0.
  - **NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`.** It refused with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3) because it needs every package built (`packages/plugins/organizations/dist` is absent). A repo-wide `pnpm build` is CI's run. This diff changes no build config, `exports` or package manifest.

## Acceptance notes

- **The two sentences this change makes false are rewritten in this PR** (seat answer 6100715923, claim surface amended): `examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/approver-bindings.flow.ts:9-17` (position is a registry binding committed by machine name) and `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx:336-339` (position decision-output picker values are machine names; `department` / `team` keep record ids).
- `ApprovalEscalationSchema.escalateTo` carries `xRef: { kind: 'position' }` with no `sources`. objectui resolves its picker through the same spec-derived fallback, so it follows the binding with the C9 follow-up. No spec change is needed there.
- `ApproverValueBinding`'s `record` member keeps `valueField: 'id' | 'name'`, although no record binding commits `name` now. Narrowing a published type for no reader would be churn.
